balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For SATS Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For SATS Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For SATS Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For SATS Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For SATS Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

flightsShips.title: Flights handled and ship calls handled
flightsShips.content:
Flights handled is the number of aircraft turnarounds SATS services at the airports where it operates ground handling (gateway services, baggage, ramp). Ship calls handled is the number of vessel calls serviced by SATS's marine/port logistics business.

For SATS Ltd.: these are the physical-volume drivers behind Revenue in the Gateway Services segment -- a flight-volume recovery (post-COVID) or airline-contract win shows up here before it shows up in the margin lines, since ground handling is largely a fixed-cost, high-volume-leverage business.

What to watch:

  • Flight volume versus regional air-traffic recovery (Changi Airport throughput)
  • Ship calls as a smaller, separate volume line -- do not read it as a proxy for flights
  • Revenue per flight/ship-call trend, since neither volume line alone explains margin

mealsProduced.title: Meals produced: aviation vs non-aviation
mealsProduced.content:
Aviation meals is inflight catering produced for airline customers; non-aviation meals is food produced for non-airline customers (institutional catering, Food Solutions Group, Asia Airfreight Terminal). Gross meals produced is the total.

For SATS Ltd.: the non-aviation share (now over a third of volume) is the diversification thesis -- it reduces SATS's dependence on airline travel demand, which is the single biggest swing factor in the Gateway Services segment.

What to watch:

  • Non-aviation share of total meal volume rising over time (diversification working)
  • Aviation meal volume versus flights handled -- a mismatch implies a change in meals-per-flight or catering contract mix
  • Only FY2024-FY2026 are disclosed in the KPI tables; do not extrapolate the trend further back

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For SATS Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For SATS Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For SATS Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For SATS Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For SATS Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
